issues.description: The problem statement UML defines numberOfInscribedStudents as an int, but the solution implementation declares numberOfInscribedStudents as a long (and the constructor parameter uses long). The template leaves attributes unspecified, so students will follow the UML and implement an int. This type mismatch between the UML/specification and the solution is structural and may confuse students about the correct attribute type and lead to inconsistent code or failing tests. Additionally, getTotalNumberOfStudents() is specified in the UML to return int, but the solution sums a long and an int and returns an int, introducing an implicit narrowing that conflicts with the UML's int-based design.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute types consistent across all artifacts. Either change the solution to declare numberOfInscribedStudents as int (and update the constructor, getter, setter, and toString accordingly) to match the UML, or update the UML/problem statement to specify long for numberOfInscribedStudents and adjust the return type/comments for getTotalNumberOfStudents if necessary. Prefer keeping all integer student-count fields the same primitive type to avoid implicit narrowing and student confusion.
